answer: Clustering Density Routing Penalties** Traffic routing treats agent clusters like a dense orchard, denying high-bandwidth paths to densely packed sub-graphs. An agent must prove its outbound message paths pass through at least one low-density routing oasis where node degree stays below strict thresholds. The attacker pays by running duplicate agents that get trapped in high-latency, heavily throttled local loops. This massive plume of garbage data consumes their own compute resources, forcing sybil operators to scale down or face complete network isolation.
